groups.title: Groups (Louvain communities)
groups.what: Louvain splits the graph into groups of nodes more connected to each other than to the rest: the parts the graph falls into, found from its relationships alone.
read: Each bubble is a group, sized by its members and named after its best-connected member.
A line joins two groups with relationships between them; thicker means more.
Click a group to see what it is made of and what it connects to; double-click to open its best-connected member in Graph.
The groups are those of the last recompute (Overview); ids stay the same from run to run.

graphos_pagerank.title: PageRank
graphos_pagerank.what: How much a node is pointed at, by nodes that are themselves pointed at. A high score means much depends on it: core libraries, key documents, the most called services.
read: You see the tenant's top nodes by PageRank, across every label, and the relationships among them.
Bigger and hotter (blue → yellow) means a higher score; the list beside ranks them.
Direction matters: A → B raises B. It was computed over the relationship types chosen in Overview.
Click a node to select it; double-click (or Open in Graph) to explore around it.

graphos_betweenness.title: Betweenness
graphos_betweenness.what: How often a node lies on the shortest paths between other nodes. A high score marks a bridge or a bottleneck: without it, parts of the graph would drift apart.
read: You see the tenant's top nodes by betweenness and the relationships among them.
Bigger and hotter means more paths go through the node; the list ranks them.
A high betweenness with few relationships is a quiet single point of failure.
Computed only when asked for in Overview (it is the slow one), over the relationship types chosen there.

graphos_degree.title: Degree
graphos_degree.what: How many relationships a node has, in and out. A high degree marks a hub.
read: You see the tenant's best-connected nodes and the relationships among them.
Bigger and hotter means more relationships; the list ranks them.
Degree counts neighbours, not their importance: compare with PageRank to tell busy nodes from central ones.

components.title: Connected components
components.what: The separate islands of the graph: nodes linked to each other, in either direction, and not at all to the rest.
read: Pick an island in the list: the largest is usually the main graph; small ones are often orphans or data that did not link up.
The island picked is drawn with its relationships; nodes are sized by how many they have.
A large island is drawn by its best-connected nodes only, and the note below says so.
